clue.text: Spirit present initially in busy street musicians

indicators.note: in places the spirit and the letter inside the shuffled street
a busy scene is all bustle and jumble, so the letters of street are stirred up

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word present

explanation.surface: A ghostly presence turns up among the buskers on a crowded high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' makes TETERS from STREET; RUM plus P (first of 'present') goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of a brass instrument are musicians by trade or hobby.

clue.text: This one's off before reckless party

indicators.note: off says the letters that follow are removed from the word before them

parts.note: one is I, and the 's stands for is, giving IS
rash means reckless, acting without thought

explanation.surface: Someone declares an item cancelled ahead of a wild get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' reads as 'one is', I plus S; with IS taken 'off' THIS leaves TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a big lively celebration with dancing and drink is called this.

clue.text: What in Madrid coming after university is incomparable

indicators.note: coming after puts the Spanish word behind the short form of university

parts.note: que is the Spanish word for what, as spoken in Madrid

explanation.surface: A Spanish-speaking student asks about a peerless college.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one of a kind cannot be matched or compared with anything else.

clue.text: Work in the theatre, creating an appearance

definitions.text: Work in the theatre, creating an appearance

parts.words: Work in the theatre, creating an appearance
parts.note: the theatre is an operating theatre, not a stage, and the appearance created is a reshaped face or body

explanation.surface: Reads as stagecraft: an actor making an entrance on the boards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic operations by surgeons alter how a patient looks.

clue.text: Classified source of energy found in new crop test

indicators.note: found in places the single letter inside the reworked letters
new says the letters of crop test are made into a fresh arrangement
the source of a word is where it starts, so its first letter

explanation.surface: A secret energy supply turns up in an agricultural trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives E, which is 'found in' the shuffle of CROP TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Documents restricted to authorised people only carry this security grading.

clue.text: Suffers after runs and horizontal bars

indicators.note: after puts the word for suffers behind the abbreviation for runs

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
ails means suffers or is unwell

explanation.surface: A gymnast is hurting after running and working on the bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Fences and banisters are made of long level bars like these.

clue.text: Graduate teacher's furniture items?

definitions.meaning: a B.Ed., Bachelor of Education, is a teaching graduate, with the possessive 's
pieces of bedroom furniture to sleep on

explanation.surface: Asks what tables and chairs a newly qualified teacher owns.
explanation.walkthrough: B.Ed. is the British teaching degree, Bachelor of Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping furniture pieces, and also the abbreviated degree plus possessive.

clue.text: European in motion to accept English court is optional

indicators.note: to accept says the word for in motion takes the other letters inside

parts.note: live in the sense of active, moving, in operation

explanation.surface: A European proposal brought to an English court is voluntary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in motion' means active or working, as a live wire or live broadcast is in operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A course or procedure one may choose to take is elective, not compulsory.

clue.text: Extract from essay on a race so long?

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A student pulls a passage from a lengthy essay about a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese farewell, used in English as goodbye.

clue.text: The point of African optimism

parts.note: point means a headland, an African one named for good hope, which is optimism

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what Africa's hopefulness is for.
explanation.definitionFit: The headland at South Africa's tip bears a name meaning optimistic expectation.

clue.text: Artist volunteers to eat one side order

indicators.note: to eat says the pair takes the numeral inside, as if swallowing it

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A painter and some reservists share a curry-house extra.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer army.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoghurt and cucumber dish served beside Indian food is ordered on the side.

clue.text: Hobby that's hip, possibly in the recent past

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of hip could appear in another order

parts.note: lately means recently, in the recent past

explanation.surface: Wonders whether some pastime has become fashionable of late.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp collecting is a classic pastime.

clue.text: Sink fuel container

definitions.meaning: a coal bucket kept by the fireplace

explanation.surface: Kitchen basin and petrol can make an odd pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is deliberately holing a vessel; the noun is a coal hod.

clue.text: Fancying and cooking stew with one

indicators.note: cooking works the letters of stew and one into a new mix

explanation.surface: Someone likes making stew and adding a single extra ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Being attracted to someone romantically is an informal idiom for fancying them.

clue.text: Mark felt differently, always suffering from this

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: differently says the letters of felt are arranged another way

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A man named Mark has had different feelings his whole life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name; it is SCAR. 'differently' makes LEFT from FELT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacterial illness with a red rash; the clue's 'this' points to the disease being suffered.

clue.text: Create a diversion in harbour

definitions.meaning: to harbour a thought is to hold or consider it

explanation.surface: Like a smuggler distracting the coastguard at the port.
explanation.definitionFit: Both amusing guests and holding an idea in mind are senses of the verb.

clue.text: Conned crossing threshold, conflicted

indicators.note: crossing says the word for conned spans the word for threshold, holding it inside

parts.note: did is slang for swindled, as in 'they did him out of his money'
a verge is an edge or brink, a threshold

explanation.surface: A trickster stepped over someone's doorstep and caused a clash.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions that split apart and disagree have gone separate ways.

clue.text: Runs from moaner on board ship

indicators.note: on board places the complainer inside the letters for ship

parts.note: SS is steamship
a carper is someone who finds fault and moans

explanation.surface: Someone flees a grumbling passenger on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' is a verb here: scarper is British slang for run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away quickly is slang-flavoured fleeing.

clue.text: Hard coat produced by processing cast iron unit

indicators.note: processing works the letters of cast iron unit into a new form

explanation.surface: A foundry unit making cast iron leaves a hard crust.
explanation.definitionFit: A crust or hard deposit built up on a surface.

clue.text: Stick around at home for the dog

indicators.note: around says the stick goes round the word for at home

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
in means at home, not out

explanation.surface: Keep a walking stick handy at home for the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means any member of the dog family.

clue.text: Arrival of express after a day

indicators.note: after puts the word for express behind the first two letters

parts.note: to vent feelings is to express them

explanation.surface: An express train turns up a day late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' looks like a fast train; it is the verb VENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming or arriving, as in the advent of spring.

clue.text: Furious tabloid in terrible need

indicators.note: in places the newspaper inside the jumbled letters
terrible signals the letters of need in a bad mess

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A furious tabloid campaign about dire poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' makes ENED from NEED; RAG goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made very angry is a synonym for furious.

clue.text: Body language revealing Nobel prize winner

indicators.note: revealing says the letters are shown within the words body language

explanation.surface: A laureate's posture gives the game away.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob, the songwriter, won the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature.

clue.text: Off colour, playing football?

parts.note: off colour looks like feeling unwell, but it is the colour of the card that sends a player off

explanation.surface: Feeling poorly while playing a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee shows this scarlet card to dismiss a footballer.

clue.text: Fighter freed irregular, almost capturing student

indicators.note: capturing says the jumble takes the student letter inside
freed lets the remaining letters loose into a new order
almost says the word irregular loses its last letter

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, so student

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter released an irregular soldier who had nearly caught a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims IRREGULAR to IRREGULA; 'freed' rearranges those letters, and L goes inside ('capturing').
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an irregular band waging small-scale warfare is this kind of fighter.

clue.text: Love stay in Scotland — such colour

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
in Scottish usage to stay somewhere means to live there

explanation.surface: An invitation to romance and a Scottish holiday with a matching shade.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland 'where do you stay?' means 'where do you live?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull greenish shade is named after the fruit.

clue.text: Homer's expression, holding onto son for money

indicators.note: holding onto says the catchphrase contains the single letter

parts.note: Homer Simpson's catchphrase is d'oh

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson exclaims as he hangs onto his boy for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' is the cartoon dad, not the Greek poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang synonym for cash, heard in everyday informal speech.

clue.text: An all-rounder's chance is here, no matter what happens

definitions.meaning: a decathlete or all-rounder could win whichever discipline is contested

explanation.surface: An athlete good at everything has a shot at winning whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means regardless or whatever the case, and literally describes a versatile competitor.
